summary: Ships crossing the widening stress field encounter visible harmonic tearing as their hulls cast delayed, fractured reflections in open space.
panelPlan: Full-width space panel: several ships cross a corridor field whose stars and beacon reflections shear sideways, with one vessel trailing a delayed version of its own silhouette.
Interior/exterior paired panel: the captain reports the impossible reflection while Liora and Alan compare the ship's stable hull telemetry to unstable corridor geometry.
Final wide panel lets the distortion itself dominate the page as the delayed silhouettes multiply across more than one vessel.
directionInline: Escalate from one trailing silhouette to a field-wide navigational hazard affecting multiple ships.

dialogueInline.text: Control, the stars are moving sideways.
I was happier before you said that.

summary: Liora tries to hold ships still long enough to map the distortion, warning that movement through folded lane geometry could make the readings—and casualties—worse.
panelPlan: Liora receives overlapping ship feeds from the damaged network.
She freezes a distortion map and orders the reporting ship to keep engines idle.
The captain’s vessel drifts relative to a corridor marker even without thrust.
End on Liora trying to construct one stable geometry from contradictory positions.
directionInline: Her instruction is a controlled response to unknown geometry, not passivity.

dialogueInline.text: Then what exactly am I holding?
Whatever the corridor still agrees is your position.

summary: Alan realizes even idling ships are unsafe because the anchor points themselves are slipping.
panelPlan: Alan compares the ship’s fixed engine state to the moving anchor reference.
A supposedly stationary reference marker jumps between positions.
Liora sees that navigation cannot solve a failure of the coordinate frame.
End on the map losing another reliable anchor as Alan states the problem.
directionInline: This closes the possibility that skilled pilots can simply wait out the crisis.

dialogueInline.text: Navigation is honest. Space changed underneath it.

summary: At Orban Port, every departure board closes in cascading waves and civilians finally see the transport network stop functioning.
panelPlan: Wide concourse with boards graying out row by row above packed travelers.
People look for alternate gates only to watch those close too.
The concerned traveler from earlier finds no live route at all.
End on the question of where the ships have gone.
directionInline: Use visual continuity with earlier Orban scenes so the loss of normal function is obvious.

dialogueInline.text: There aren't any alternates on the board.
Stop watching the board. Stay where staff can find you.

summary: Port staff can no longer offer routing answers; Ava keeps the crowd together because any future opening will be useless if people scatter.
panelPlan: A staffer asks civilians to remain in the concourse while internal route tools also show uncertainty.
A few travelers begin moving toward exits or restricted access points.
Ava steps into the flow and physically turns people back toward a common waiting zone.
End on the crowd staying together because of Ava, not because the boards recovered.
directionInline: Shift authority from system information to trusted human presence.

dialogueInline.text: I have nothing to route them on.
Keep families together. Clear the doors. Make one waiting zone.
Then we use the first real opening we get.

summary: Owen attempts formal corridor lockouts from the old BHA command floor and discovers that the authority channels no longer respond.
panelPlan: Establish the former BHA command floor under emergency lighting.
Owen sends a standard lockout across multiple approaches.
Every command returns dead authority or silent red failure.
End on Owen recognizing that his procedural control no longer reaches the network.
directionInline: The failure is institutional and technical at once: the command exists, but nothing answers it.

summary: Lochran demands that Owen enforce closures anyway, clinging to boundaries that the physical system can no longer recognize.
panelPlan: Lochran joins or calls into the failed command floor demanding closure enforcement.
Owen demonstrates that the lockout requests are not merely delayed but unregistered.
Lochran points to the mapped corridor boundaries as if authority can restore them.
End on a map line remaining crisp while the live status beneath it goes blank.
directionInline: Make the gap between mapped authority and physical reality explicit.

dialogueInline.text: A pilot can't crash into a law, Chair.
Not if they never receive it.

summary: A major convergence node begins physically detaching, turning network failure into a structural disaster with people still aboard.
panelPlan: Large reveal panel: a major convergence node begins physically separating along one structural arm while occupied sections remain attached and people are still moving through them.
Inside the node, Alan and Owen see the arm's displacement cross the evacuation threshold; the captain confirms people remain in the lower section.
Final panel gives the failing joint major visual scale as evacuation lights come on across the still-occupied arm.
directionInline: Give the convergence-node collapse major visual scale while keeping occupied sections and evacuation stakes readable.

dialogueInline.text: There are still people on that section.
Then don't ask me how much.

summary: Alan organizes immediate evacuation from the failing arm while debris starts to fill the junction.
panelPlan: Alan converts a traffic display into an evacuation map.
Survivors move toward the remaining stable connection while structural panels tear free behind them.
Rescue craft try to hold relative position in a drifting debris field.
End on the last group reaching the junction as the arm moves out of alignment.
directionInline: Keep the rescue procedural and physical, not abstract.

dialogueInline.text: Use the maintenance spine. Leave everything else.
Cut them loose if you have to.
Rescue two has the last group.
Get them across before the joint turns.

summary: Owen discovers he cannot close the approach, leaving incoming pilots to enter a dead junction without authoritative warning.
panelPlan: Owen repeatedly sends closure commands through failing channels.
Incoming craft remain visible on approach vectors that should have been blocked.
He attempts direct contact as the automated authority path dies.
End on one incoming ship crossing the point where a functioning lockout would have stopped it.
directionInline: This pays off the dead-authority problem from Pages 6–7.

dialogueInline.text: Two ships. They think the junction is open.
One just crossed the old stop line.

summary: A blinded incoming captain asks for manual guidance as the shattered node spins and Alan becomes the human replacement for the failed network.
panelPlan: Inside the incoming ship, nav references collapse into contradictory vectors.
The captain calls for guidance before the ship enters the node’s spin.
Alan finds one surviving beacon and gives a narrow manual path through the debris.
End on the ship committing to the improvised guidance while the broken node turns around it.
directionInline: The transition from centralized automation to person-to-person rescue should be unmistakable.

dialogueInline.text: Node control, nav is gone. Give me something.
You have one beacon. Keep it two degrees port.
From the only thing in there that isn't moving.

summary: Ava chooses a partially functional Sector 9 route because the medical convoy cannot wait for a fully verified corridor.
panelPlan: Back at Orban, Ava identifies one intermittent path among otherwise dead routes.
Medicine pallets are loaded while the route flickers between open and unknown.
Ava weighs the route against the destination’s medical need.
End on the convoy preparing for Sector 9 despite no guarantee.
directionInline: Stage Ava's choice against visible medicine crates and an intermittently available route; the guaranteed harm of waiting must be readable without explanatory text.

dialogueInline.text: No confirmation from the far end.

summary: The traffic controller warns that Sector 9 may not even know it is open, but Ava commits to the gamble because waiting guarantees loss.
panelPlan: The controller shows intermittent alignment with no confirmation from the far end.
Ava steadies against the console as the port floor vibrates under another distant failure.
The convoy crew look to Ava rather than the system for the go/no-go choice.
End on the first medical ship entering the uncertain route.
directionInline: Finish on action: Ava’s model of authority is becoming practical trust under uncertainty.

dialogueInline.text: You may arrive to a closed corridor.
If we wait, they arrive to an empty pharmacy.
Then why are you still here?
I wanted one person to know where we went.

summary: Outer Ring habitats lose power in sections as severed corridor links destabilize life-support distribution.
panelPlan: Wide outer habitat cycling from light to darkness in uneven sections.
Ruben’s crew sees atmosphere and power loads spike across local systems.
A major conduit bucks under the surge.
End on Ruben warning that one more hit could drop atmosphere.
directionInline: Keep the threat domestic and bodily: light, air, pressure.

dialogueInline.text: Power's dropping on the same leg.
One more surge and we lose the ring.
Then we don't give it one more surge.

summary: With no central help coming, outer workers brace the grid manually using whatever material remains.
panelPlan: The outer technician rejects waiting for remote assistance and starts stripping usable support material nearby.
Ruben redirects workers to a failing conduit while others isolate nonessential loads.
Improvised braces take strain as the habitat remains partially powered.
End on the crew holding the system together by hand.
directionInline: Keep the repair improvised, local, and materially grounded: mismatched braces, hand tools, and worn outer infrastructure; do not introduce mature post-Break faction insignia.

dialogueInline.text: My plan is this brace, that cutoff, and six people who showed up.
Finally, a plan I can touch.

summary: The Council gathers inside a communications storm while Lochran still argues that projecting command is essential to preventing panic.
panelPlan: Wide Council chamber with overlapping alarms, broken feeds, and delegates receiving contradictory world reports.
Lochran tries to reestablish a single command channel and calls for visible authority.
Several world feeds drop while he speaks.
End on the chamber unable to behave like one center anymore.
directionInline: Play both truths at once: social panic is dangerous, and the old command structure is no longer capable of containing the physical crisis.

dialogueInline.text: One command channel. We need people hearing the same thing.
They are not living the same thing.

summary: Iskara directly links the cost of denial to the growing casualty reports, making the leadership fracture irreversible.
panelPlan: Iskara brings casualty and failure reports into the same space as Lochran’s command plan.
She confronts him at close range rather than through procedural debate.
Delegates around them stop pretending this is a normal Council disagreement.
End on Lochran’s practiced composure finally cracking.
directionInline: This is moral accusation grounded in consequences already shown.

dialogueInline.text: Orban is rationing movement. Outer is rationing air. Broken Node is pulling bodies out by hand.
Then stop talking as if this room still runs them.
Someone has to hold the center.
There is no center left to hold.

summary: Damian abandons any hope of one unified message and pushes for whatever local guidance each world can still receive.
panelPlan: Damian scans world channels with different needs and different surviving capabilities.
He stops editing one central statement and begins routing practical guidance outward.
Lochran and Iskara remain divided behind him while the communications work becomes decentralized.
End on multiple separate world messages leaving the chamber instead of one Cooperative broadcast.
directionInline: Show Damian changing what he does, not only what he believes.

dialogueInline.text: I'm sending local guidance by world.
A unified statement can't tell Outer how to brace a conduit.
If it's useful, it survives. If it isn't, the logo won't save it.

summary: Alan and surviving captains establish an ad-hoc rescue cluster around one temporarily stable pocket in the distorted field.
panelPlan: Establish a calm pocket surrounded by visibly warped corridor space and drifting debris.
Alan anchors rescue traffic to one surviving beacon rather than the dead network.
Captains take assigned sectors and move toward scattered survivors.
End on the first rescue craft crossing into the pocket.
directionInline: The rescue cluster is a practical replacement for centralized routing.

dialogueInline.text: Long enough is the measurement today.
Take sector two. I'll feed you debris drift.

summary: Rescuers pull survivors from debris while the stable pocket shifts around them.
panelPlan: Rescue craft crosses the temporary pocket boundary.
Debris shifts and forces a second craft to roll away.
Two survivors transfer across a maintenance tether.
The stable pocket contracts on Alan's live map.
A captain reports four people still outside the line; Alan refuses to reduce the count to fit the time.
Final panel: the rescue craft turns back toward the moving boundary.
directionInline: Keep action readable and spatially coherent.

dialogueInline.text: We have four survivors outside the line.

summary: The captain warns that another pocket shift could scatter rescuers into null space, but the cluster stays long enough to recover the last reachable people.
panelPlan: The captain watches the pocket boundary move against the beacon.
Alan orders the last transfer completed before withdrawal.
A final survivor is pulled aboard as the field distorts across the rescue path.
End on the cluster breaking formation and escaping just before the pocket shifts.
directionInline: The rescue succeeds locally while the larger system continues failing.

summary: Liora watches the final five network nodes die in synchrony and understands that the Cooperative Network itself is gone.
panelPlan: Nearly full-page panel: Liora watches five remaining network nodes blink out one by one across an otherwise dark system map, each loss leaving more empty space than the last.
Small final panel: the last trace disappears and Liora is left reflected in a dead display.
